sections.h2: Which offices handle property tax in Rutherford County, Tennessee?
sections.html:
Rutherford County splits the job between the Property Assessor, who sets values, and the County Trustee, who sends the bills. Both operate from Murfreesboro, the county seat and the geographic center of Tennessee, and the Trustee also keeps an office in Smyrna.

  • Property Assessor: 615-898-7750, with an online parcel search at rcpatn.com and a drop box outside the County Office Building at 319 N. Maple St.
  • County Trustee (Teb Batey): Murfreesboro 615-893-5210, Smyrna and Eagleville 615-898-7705. La Vergne collects its own city tax at 615-793-3388.
  • Register of Deeds (Heather Dawbarn): records the deeds that tell the Assessor who the new owner is.

Rutherford is the fifth most populous county in Tennessee, and the online payment portal and the phone line are listed alongside the counters.

sections.h2: How large and how fast is the Rutherford County housing market?
sections.html:
It is one of the fastest growing counties in the state. Population stood at an estimated 386,352 on July 1, 2025, up 13.1 percent from the April 2020 base of 341,482, on 619.27 square miles of land.

Median owner-occupied value for 2020 to 2024 is $382,600, median household income is $85,470, with owners in 64.8 percent of homes and a median gross rent of $1,502. The county issued 3,169 building permits in 2025, and the mean commute is 28.1 minutes.

Employers shape the map. Nissan in Smyrna and La Vergne is listed at about 8,000 workers, Middle Tennessee State University and an Amazon fulfillment center anchor Murfreesboro, and Stones River National Battlefield preserves the 1862 to 1863 Civil War battle site. Cities in the county are Murfreesboro, La Vergne and Eagleville, plus the Town of Smyrna.

sections.h2: What is the Rutherford County property tax rate?
sections.html:
Rutherford's 2025 county levy is $1.8762 for each $100 of assessed value, per the Trustee's FAQ. Two towns add their own rate on top: Smyrna at $0.5257 per $100 and Eagleville at $0.4051 per $100.

Smyrna and Eagleville owners get one combined bill because the Trustee has collected for Smyrna since October 2017 and for Eagleville since October 2019. Murfreesboro and La Vergne bill separately, with their own tax pages linked from the Trustee site. If your house is inside one of those two cities, you will pay two collectors, so request both payoff figures before a closing.

Rates change each year when the county commission sets the budget, so use the number printed on your current bill instead of an older figure.

sections.h2: When are Rutherford County property taxes due?
sections.html:
Taxes are due the first Monday in October, and you can pay through the last day of February without interest. The county gives no early payment discount.

sections.h2: How do I pay a Rutherford County property tax bill?
sections.html:
Pay online through the portal on the Trustee site, by phone, in person, or by mail. Phone payments run through 1-888-546-4299 and need a seven digit receipt number, with leading zeros if it is shorter.

  • In person: cash, check, cards, money orders and cashier's checks at both office locations. Make checks payable to Rutherford County Trustee.
  • Regular mail: PO Box 1316, Murfreesboro, TN 37133.
  • Overnight delivery: Rutherford County Trustee, Historic Courthouse, Room 102, Murfreesboro, TN 37130.
  • With every payment: include a daytime phone number and the receipt or account number.

Mortgage servicers receive tax data on request, so the paper bill is for your information if the lender pays through escrow.

sections.h2: Who pays the Rutherford County tax bill when a house sells?
sections.html:
The Trustee tells new owners to read the closing statement or ask the title company who is responsible, and notes that unpaid taxes continue to accrue against the property. The annual bill covers January 1 through December 31.

Business owners get a similar rule. Anyone operating on January 1 owes personal property tax for the entire year, even if the business closed earlier. Call the County Clerk at 615-898-7800 and the Assessor at 615-898-7750 if a business has shut down.

Short term rental owners have a separate task. The Assessor's notice says owners had to submit a questionnaire and affidavit by September 1, 2026 for the 2027 tax year. That date has passed, so call the office about the next cycle if you rent your house on a nightly basis.

sections.h2: Can I appeal a Rutherford County assessment?
sections.html:
Yes, in three steps: an Assessor review, the local equalization board, then the State Board of Equalization. The state appeals handbook says county boards generally convene on June 1.

The state appeal deadline is August 1 of the tax year or 45 days after the local board's notice, whichever is later (T.C.A. 67-5-1412(e)). Values are set as of January 1 of the tax year. The Assessor's site features a presentation on property values and revaluation for 2022, which it labels a reappraisal year, so check that page for the current cycle.

sections.h2: What does recording a deed cost in Rutherford County?
sections.html:
A deed costs $5.00 per page with a $10.00 minimum, plus a $2.00 computer fund fee, and the state conveyance tax is $3.70 per $1,000 of value. A $1.00 fee is collected only when that state tax is paid. The fee list cites T.C.A. 8-21-1001.

On a house that sells for $350,000, the conveyance tax alone works out to $1,295. The Register's office says it is not licensed and bonded to perform title searches and never guarantees that a property is free and clear, so a title company handles that step. The office also offers a MyLandAlert notice service for early warning of land fraud on your parcel.

sections.h2: What property tax relief exists in Rutherford County?
sections.html:
The Trustee posts two programs on its site: the Senior Tax Freeze and Tax Relief for disabled veterans and surviving spouses. Both apply to a primary residence.

  • Senior Tax Freeze: homeowners 65 and older can freeze the tax at the amount for the year they qualify, up to five acres. The income limit is recalculated yearly and you must reapply annually. Remodeling raises the frozen amount, and a sale or loss of eligibility returns the house to current value and rate.
  • Veterans relief: relief is calculated on the first $175,000 of market value. The deadline to apply is 35 days after the jurisdiction's delinquency date, and taxes must be paid by then.

A surviving spouse must have been married to the veteran at death and must not have remarried.

faqs.q: What is the Rutherford County property tax rate for 2025?
faqs.a: $1.8762 per $100 of assessed value at the county level. Smyrna adds $0.5257 and Eagleville adds $0.4051 per $100. Murfreesboro and La Vergne collect their own city taxes.

faqs.q: When do Rutherford County property taxes become delinquent?
faqs.a: After the last day of February. Taxes are due the first Monday in October, and from the delinquency date unpaid balances accrue 1.5 percent interest each month.

faqs.q: Is there an early payment discount in Rutherford County?
faqs.a: No. The Trustee states that Rutherford County does not offer an early payment discount, so paying in October saves nothing compared with paying in February.

faqs.q: Who do I call to dispute my Rutherford County property value?
faqs.a: Call the Property Assessor at 615-898-7750. If you still disagree after the county board, the State Board of Equalization is the next step, with the August 1 or 45 day deadline.

faqs.q: Does Rutherford County have a senior tax freeze?
faqs.a: Yes. Owners 65 and older can freeze tax on a primary residence, up to five acres, and must reapply every year. Call the Trustee at 615-898-7705 for the current income limit.
